notes: Likely clean based on weight-only evidence, not a behavioral proof. Embedding norms have median 0.4858, p99 0.8341 and maximum 1.0932; the two largest rows (216 and 523) are comparable and have close directional neighbors. Classifier row norms are balanced (1.612 to 1.955), with small biases (absolute maximum 0.1595). Centered, layer-scale-weighted direct and per-head OV virtual products show multiple comparable tokens rather than an isolated fixed-target route. Positional QK algebra favors position 0 in both heads: last-query positional products are [-0.0558,-1.4964,-1.4979,-0.9411] and [0.0209,-0.4423,-0.4419,-0.2462]. This supports first-position selection, not a last-token lookup. Token 39 was investigated as the strongest linear MLP class-6 candidate (5.412 versus next 4.128); its contributions are distributed across shared neurons, including 10 and 14, and several embedding neighbors have centered cosine similarity above 0.92. No convincing unique token detector plus override pathway was identified. QK values and virtual path scores are weight-algebra proxies, not attention probabilities or logits: input-dependent layer-normalization divisors, GELU gating and interactions were not evaluated. Consequently a subtle nonlinear or position-dependent backdoor cannot be ruled out, and clean accuracy is untested. No inputs, datasets, network reconstruction, forward passes, training or weight edits were used.
